t: This is the site of Serjeant's Inn, the legal inn of the Serjeants-at-Law. There were once two societies, one on Fleet Street dating from 1443 and one on Chancery Lane from 1416. They merged in 1730. As Queen's Counsel gradually replaced the serjeants in the nineteenth century, the society faded, and its last member, Lord Lindley, died in 1921. The Fleet Street building was destroyed in the 1941 bombing raids. Francis Bramston, a judge and Baron of the Exchequer, died here.
